$comment: The self-probe gate's cost ceiling, in seconds, checked in CI against the evidence the probe already writes. Raising this is a reviewable diff with a reason, which is the entire point: the gate went from 9.6 to 23.6 minutes across one merged pull request and nothing said a word. Growth is allowed; going unnoticed is not. Budget the TOTAL and never a per-fault average — the regression that prompted this raised the fault count from 59 to 91 while per-fault cost barely moved, so an average would have reported everything fine.
headroom: The local figure (804 s) is what a developer sees; the CI figure (906 s before #82, 962 s after) is what the check runs against, and a CI runner is ~13% slower than the idle machine above. The first budget was 18% over the LOCAL figure and only 4.6% over the CI one, so the first PR to add any claim tripped it. 1100 is ~14% over the CI measurement: an ordinary run never flaps; a 59-to-91 style jump (+76%) still fails. Budget against the from-scratch CI number, never a run that reused verdicts — the release job probes from scratch.

history.why: First budget. Set from the 804 s measurement after #73 cut the gate from 1414 s.

#82 added eight unit-defended faults (~30 s in CI) and main went 906 -> 981 s from scratch, red against 950. Re-pointing the two replay-defended calibration claims onto pure tests took it to 962 s. The remaining overage was the budget itself: set 18% over a local 804 s, it was 4.6% over the 906 s CI already measured. Raised to 1100 against the CI figure. The heavy claims it names — TG-ADMIT-NEEDS-ALL-KILLED 87 s, TG-PROBE-NEVER-EDITS-THE-TREE-IT-MEASURES 70 s, the two TG-MCP-* at 42 s — are the next #73-style cut, tracked separately.
